text: GRC tooling gets talked about like it's a single magic product that makes compliance effortless. It isn't one product, and it doesn't make the judgment calls effortless at all. This lesson breaks down the real categories of GRC tooling and draws a hard line around what they actually automate versus what they can't.

Platform GRC suites like RSA Archer and ServiceNow GRC centralize risk registers, control libraries, and policy documents for large organizations running many frameworks at once. Automated evidence platforms like Vanta, Drata, and Secureframe connect directly to cloud infrastructure and continuously pull evidence instead of waiting on a human. Policy management and attestation platforms handle distributing documents, collecting signatures, and tracking who hasn't acknowledged the current version. Knowing the category tells you what a given tool is actually built to do.

Control-to-framework mapping is the direct software answer to mapping one control once instead of three times. A platform maintains a crosswalk showing which requirement in SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS a given control satisfies. Assess the control once, and the tool shows it satisfied everywhere it maps. That mapping decision is still a human judgment call, made once by someone qualified — the tool's job is remembering and reapplying it.

Automated evidence collection replaces weeks of manually screenshotting IAM policies and emailing zip files to an auditor, pulling today's actual configuration instead of a stale annual snapshot — that's continuous controls monitoring. Attestation tracking automates distributing a policy, collecting signatures, and flagging who hasn't responded, but it proves acknowledgment, not comprehension.

What none of this automates is the judgment underneath the bookkeeping: whether a risk is acceptable, whether an exception is reasonable, or what root cause actually explains a failed control. A tool can flag noncompliance; it can't decide what the organization does about it — which is exactly the human, cultural question Lesson 4 picks up next.
